newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-FROST CELEBRATES START OF NEW ERA.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-FROST CELEBRATES START OF NEW ERA.

text.p: Morten Frost, one of the greatest players of all time, has enjoyed another career high by steering Malaysia into division one for the first time at the world team championships.

Just three months after leaving his native Denmark to become the first European to coach an Asian team, the four-time All-England champion has helped to mark the start of a new era for Malaysian badminton.

And he achieved it despite the handicap of being without Rashid Sidek, who was ranked number one earlier this year but refused to travel with the team unless he could compete only in the individual championships.
That request that was turned down by the Badminton Association of Malaysia.
Malaysia defeated the Netherlands (3-2), Russia (3-2) and Canada (4-1) in the group matches and then secured promotion with a dramatic 3-2 win over Germany in the promotion play-off.

"I am so proud of the team," said Frost. "This was the first target when I took over and to do it without Rashid Sidek is amazing. But everyone worked very hard -- the players, the coaches -- and there was a great team spirit."

Frost was particularly proud of the Malaysian women, whose ages ranged from 15 to 20. Law Pei Pei, 17, underlined the emergence of the female force by defeating Heike Schonharting 12-10 11-6 in the promotion clash with Germany.
"I'm very pleased with the way the women played and it confirms that there is an exciting future ahead for Malaysian badminton. This is a team for the future, " Frost said.
Frost, who has a four-year contract, also hopes that the success could persuade more European coaches to head east.

"It would be good for badminton if there was more of a mix of coaching ideas," he said. "It is a tremendous challenge for me to have gone to Malaysia. The people, the language and the culture are so different. But I'm learning quickly and I think it is good to be flexible, and be able to adapt.
"I couldn't have asked for a better debut as Malaysian coach. Hopefully it is just the start," Frost added.
